evidence: "m = n-1"; "DFS to find edges that are part of minimal subtree connecting terminals"; the other survivors also build an adjacency tree and mark terminal vertices
affordance_in_statement: The full list of proposed constraints is comprehensive enough that, if every single one were active, all n variables would be forced to share one identical value. ... m = n − 1.
removal_suggestion: There is no legal wording-only removal: with n vertices, n−1 pairwise equality edges, and guaranteed global connectivity, the instance is intrinsically a tree, so the answer is necessarily the sum of the edges in the unique subtree spanning the observables. It would require changing the graph model or allowing a non-tree number of constraints.

common_affordance: The constraints form a connected tree, so connecting all observables has a unique required subtree and needs no general Steiner-tree search.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its Kruskal-style process can select cheap edges outside the observable-terminal subtree before the terminals become connected, thereby charging irrelevant branches instead of summing exactly the unique required subtree.

recommended_edit: No valid edit exists under the immutable constraints. To defeat all survivors, the task would need to stop guaranteeing a connected graph with exactly n−1 pairwise edges—for example, permit a general connected graph with redundant constraints—so the problem becomes a genuine weighted Steiner-tree problem.
regression_risk: Any attempt to weaken only the wording while retaining m=n−1 and global connectivity will leave the same tree reduction intact.
